question: What do ASRS or NTSB incident reports say about DJI Matrice 4T lost-link events?
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.reason: ASRS or NTSB incident reports about lost-link events and recommended pilot actions.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance: if the control link is lost, attempt to reestablish the link; if unsuccessful, initiate emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link. FAA guidance (transfer of operational control) states that transfer between certificated remote pilots requires both to maintain Visual Line of Sight without loss of control. Manuals: there is no usable evidence for DJI Matrice 4T in the approved collection. Incident reports: no usable evidence for DJI Matrice 4T incident reports (unverified accounts). Gap/conflict: explicit ASRS/NTSB incident details for DJI Matrice 4T lost-link events to compare with FAA guidance are not available, leaving open questions about step-by-step actions, thresholds, RTH triggers, and durations.

claims.text: When the control link is lost, try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft; if the connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.
claims.quote: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.

claims.text: Transfer of operational control between certificated remote pilots is allowed only if both are capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight of the small unmanned aircraft without loss of control.
claims.quote: two or more certificated remote pilots transferring operational control (i.e., the remote PIC designation) to each other may do so only if they are both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight (VLOS) of the small unmanned aircraft without loss of control.
conditions: transfer of control between remote pilots
